device.category: 8-voice two-layer analogue polyphonic synthesiser module (desktop or 19-inch 4U rack), MIDI/MPE with polyphonic aftertouch
device.based_on: Inspired by the Yamaha CS-80 (see yamaha-cs-80); the manual says it is 'not a clone' but a revival of its sound design. Per-layer voice and shared controls follow the CS-80 programmable panel; CS-80 parameter ids are reused here for matching controls. MK1 differs mainly in lacking the SUSTAIN slider, SUSTAIN I/II switch and PANEL button, and in having an external CV input for the sub oscillator.

sources.title: Deckard's Dream MK2 Operation Manual
sources.note: File named 2.3.3; the cover says 2.3.0. Covers MK2 and most of MK1. Includes a full panel graphic (p.9) and a MIDI CC chart (pp.54-56).

sources.title: Sound On Sound review, 'Black Corporation Deckard's Dream' (MK1)
sources.note: MK1 detail: CEM3340-style VCOs (On Chip recreations); envelopes and LFO digitally generated; filter contour is IL-AL-A-D-R with zero sustain; LFO waves sine, saw, ramp, square, noise, external; coarse +6/-7 semitones; noise whiter and quieter than the CS-80; HPF less CS-80-like than the LPF; pressure less sensitive with no curve; layer II bleeds slightly into layer I; 12 V 5.8 A supply; separate Expander adds ring mod, chorus/vibrato, master sustain and CV inputs.

sources.title: Synthtopia, 'Black Corporation Intros Deckard's Dream MK2 Synthesizer' (13 Feb 2020)
sources.note: MK2 is a sleeker, lighter version keeping the MK1 engine, adding sustain mode and length controls; US$3,749; 128 presets per bank, 3 banks at launch.

sources.title: Bonedo, 'Black Corporation Deckard's Dream MK2: Der Traum geht weiter' (2020)
sources.note: Flat desktop case, rack ears by removing the cheeks; only new control vs MK1 is the Sustain slider; 384 patches at launch.

sources.title: Perfect Circuit, Black Corporation Deckard's Dream Mk2
sources.note: 12 V DC 2 A centre-positive supply; dimensions 'TBD'.

sources.title: Thomann UK, Black Corporation Deckard's Dream MKII
sources.note: 483 x 178 mm (19-inch 4U, depth not given); 256 presets (older figure); available since December 2020; GBP 4,199.

architecture.signal_path_note: Fully analogue audio path (per the manual); digitally scanned sliders, stored presets and MIDI.
architecture.polyphony_mode: 8 voice cards, each with layer I and layer II (one VCO, HPF+LPF and VCA per layer). Voice mode Poly (1-8 voices), Mono or Unison (up to 8 voices on one note). CARDS PER VOICE 2 pairs two cards per note (4-note polyphony).
architecture.patch_memory_note: 9 banks x 128 = 1152 presets: Factory (fixed), Banks 1-3 (pre-loaded, overwritable), Banks 4-8 user; 1024 writable slots. A preset stores all slider and switch positions and per-patch menu settings. PANEL mode plays the current panel.
architecture.panel_counts_note: From the panel graphic: per layer 24 sliders and 2 waveform switches; master section 23 sliders (coarse, fine, detune, FEET I and II, sub-osc FUNCTION, SPEED, VCO, VCF, VCA, MIX, BRIL, RESO, touch P.BEND, SPEED, VCO, VCF, keyboard control x4, PORT/GLISS, SUSTAIN), P/G and SUSTAIN I/II switches, TONE SELECTOR buttons UP, DOWN, ENTER, CANCEL, SHIFT, PANEL, VOLUME knob, front PHONES jack and POWER switch. FEET and FUNCTION are stepped sliders.
architecture.summary: A CS-80 style voice without the keyboard: each of 8 voices has two layers, each with a VCO (square with its own PWM LFO, saw, sine) plus noise through a 12 dB HPF and LPF with separate resonance and an IL/AL/A/D/R filter envelope; the sine bypasses the filters into an ADSR VCA. Velocity and (poly) aftertouch raise brilliance and level per layer. Shared sliders mix and detune the layers, offset brilliance and resonance, scale brightness and level across the keyboard, add velocity pitch bend and aftertouch-driven sub-oscillator modulation, set portamento/glissando and master sustain. Controlled by MIDI, poly AT or MPE.

modules.name: Layer I VCO
modules.description: VCO with square/pulse (PW 50-90%, PWM), saw and sine outputs; FEET sets octave or fifth. SOS (MK1) reports CEM3340-style VCO chips (On Chip recreations); MK2 keeps the MK1 engine per launch reports.

modules.name: Layer I PWM LFO
modules.description: Sine PWM LFO (SPEED, PWM depth); range 0.7-70 Hz by default (TIME menu). PWM MODE SYNC runs both layers from layer I SPEED.

properties.note: SOS (MK1): maximum PWM depth is lower than the CS-80's.

modules.name: Layer I noise
modules.description: White noise into the filters.

modules.name: Layer I VCO mix
modules.description: Square and saw (switched) plus noise level into the filters.

modules.name: Layer I VCF (HPF + LPF)
modules.description: Discrete 12 dB/oct high-pass then low-pass filters, each with resonance (RESH, RESL); neither self-oscillates. Cutoffs moved by the filter EG, brilliance, touch, sub oscillator and keyboard control.

properties.note: SOS (MK1): LPF closely matches the CS-80; HPF has a less pronounced effect.

modules.name: Layer I filter EG (IL-AL-A-D-R)
modules.description: Digitally generated (SOS, MK1). Starts IL below the set cutoffs, moves over A to AL, decays over D to the set cutoffs, releases over R. Maximum attack 1 s and decay/release 15 s by default (TIME menu, up to 100 s and 150 s).

modules.name: Layer I VCA
modules.description: Mixes the filtered signal (VCF LEVEL) with the unfiltered sine; ADSR; LEVEL sets the layer volume (0 is quiet, not silent).

modules.name: Layer I VCA EG (ADSR)
modules.description: ADSR; time ranges set in the TIME menu (as the filter EG).

modules.name: Layer II VCO
modules.description: VCO with square/pulse (PW 50-90%, PWM), saw and sine outputs; FEET sets octave or fifth. SOS (MK1) reports CEM3340-style VCO chips (On Chip recreations); MK2 keeps the MK1 engine per launch reports.

modules.name: Layer II PWM LFO
modules.description: Sine PWM LFO (SPEED, PWM depth); range 0.7-70 Hz by default (TIME menu). PWM MODE SYNC runs both layers from layer I SPEED.

properties.note: SOS (MK1): maximum PWM depth is lower than the CS-80's.

modules.name: Layer II noise
modules.description: White noise into the filters.

modules.name: Layer II VCO mix
modules.description: Square and saw (switched) plus noise level into the filters.

modules.name: Layer II VCF (HPF + LPF)
modules.description: Discrete 12 dB/oct high-pass then low-pass filters, each with resonance (RESH, RESL); neither self-oscillates. Cutoffs moved by the filter EG, brilliance, touch, sub oscillator and keyboard control.

properties.note: SOS (MK1): LPF closely matches the CS-80; HPF has a less pronounced effect.

modules.name: Layer II filter EG (IL-AL-A-D-R)
modules.description: Digitally generated (SOS, MK1). Starts IL below the set cutoffs, moves over A to AL, decays over D to the set cutoffs, releases over R. Maximum attack 1 s and decay/release 15 s by default (TIME menu, up to 100 s and 150 s).

modules.name: Layer II VCA
modules.description: Mixes the filtered signal (VCF LEVEL) with the unfiltered sine; ADSR; LEVEL sets the layer volume (0 is quiet, not silent).

modules.name: Layer II VCA EG (ADSR)
modules.description: ADSR; time ranges set in the TIME menu (as the filter EG).

modules.name: MIDI input and voice assigner
modules.description: Receives notes, velocity, channel or poly aftertouch or MPE, pitch bend, mod wheel, CCs and program/bank changes; assigns notes to 8 voice cards (mono, poly, unison; 1 or 2 cards per voice); portamento/glissando and sustain modes.

modules.name: Layer MIX
modules.description: Crossfades layer I and II for each voice (centre detent = equal).

modules.name: Sub oscillator (LFO)
modules.description: Sine, saw, reverse saw, square, random or sample-and-hold; per-note (POLY) or shared phase (MONO); 0.7-25 Hz by default (TIME menu 0.1-45 Hz). Depth levers to VCO, VCF and VCA; CLASSIC or EXTENDED depth.

modules.name: Output
modules.panel_section: VOLUME / rear AUDIO OUT / front PHONES
modules.description: Sum of all voices; preset volume -6 to +6 dB; VOLUME to the balanced mono AUDIO OUT and the front headphone jack (mono on both sides).

behaviours.name: Two layers per voice
behaviours.rule: Every note sounds layer I and layer II on its voice card; MIX crossfades them; DETUNE CH II thickens them; CARDS PER VOICE 2 doubles the cards per note (4-note poly).

behaviours.name: Filter envelope
behaviours.rule: IL-AL-A-D-R: start IL below the set cutoffs, move over A to AL, decay to the set cutoffs, release over R. With IL and AL at 0 it does nothing. HPF MOD sets whether the HPF follows the LPF or moves opposite.

behaviours.name: Sine bypass
behaviours.rule: Square, saw and noise pass the filters (VCF LEVEL); the sine goes straight to the VCA (SINE).

behaviours.name: Touch response
behaviours.rule: Per layer: velocity and aftertouch raise brilliance and level. Shared: velocity pitch bend, and aftertouch raising sub-oscillator speed and its VCO and VCF depth, note by note in poly AT or MPE mode.

behaviours.name: Sustain I / II
behaviours.rule: I: round-robin, every note releases independently. II: new notes cut off released ones and carry the release (as the CS-80), useful for legato lines over held chords; affects glide behaviour.

behaviours.name: Master sustain
behaviours.rule: The SUSTAIN slider changes the release of both layers independently of the VCA R sliders.

behaviours.name: Inverted sliders
behaviours.rule: Like the CS-80, some sliders are at maximum at the bottom (sub-osc and touch response sections, RESO, SUSTAIN short at bottom); centre-detent sliders (pitch, detune, MIX, BRIL, keyboard control) are neutral at centre.

behaviours.name: Stored presets and panel
behaviours.rule: A preset stores all sliders, switches and per-patch settings. Moving a slider takes over by PICK UP, MERGE or INSTANT; PANEL plays the physical panel.

behaviours.name: Adjustable ranges
behaviours.rule: Per patch: sub-oscillator 0.1-45 Hz limits (default 0.7-25), PWM LFO 0.1-100 Hz (default 0.7-70), maximum attack 1-100 s and decay/release 15-150 s, LFO depth CLASSIC or EXTENDED.

behaviours.name: Footage and MIDI keyboards
behaviours.rule: To match CS-80 pitch from a standard 61-note MIDI keyboard, set FEET one octave lower (SOS).

behaviours.name: Mono LFO
behaviours.rule: LFO MODE MONO uses one LFO started by the first note, not free-running (SOS); POLY gives each voice its own LFO.

behaviours.name: Warm-up
behaviours.rule: Oscillators take a few minutes to settle; RETUNE takes 10-20 s; full calibration after 20 minutes warm-up takes 10-15 minutes.

not_in_source: Research filled: release date and price, supply polarity, MK1 engine details (VCO chips, digital envelopes and LFO, filter character), LFO waveform history (EXT replaced by S/H), footage offset for MIDI keyboards, mono LFO behaviour. Still open: depth, VCO range, whether TOUCH SPEED is velocity or aftertouch on MK2 firmware, P/G centre position.
which mod wheel destinations noise 1/2 use as CCs
source_inconsistencies: Manual version: file named 2.3.3; the cover says 2.3.0.

Sub-oscillator waveforms: features list 'sine, saw, ramp, square and stepped random' (5); panel list 'sine, saw, ramp, square, random (Sample & Hold), or External'; FUNCTION section 'sine, saw, reverse saw, square, random, sample & hold, and external' (7); panel graphic and CC 104 have six positions (sine, saw, reverse saw, square, RND, S/H).
Touch response SPEED: panel list (41) says aftertouch speeds up the LFO; the TOUCH RESPONSE section says velocity. The panel graphic groups SPEED under 'SUB OSC AFTER', so aftertouch is modelled.
LPF: panel list (9) says 'Set to Low, the filter is completely open'; the VCF section says top is open and bottom closed.
P/G switch: described as 3-position (P, no glide, G) but drawn with only P and G.
FEET: the panel list gives '2 1/3'' for a fifth above 4'; the FEET section and graphic give 2 2/3'.
PWM MAX/MIN are said to set the top and bottom of the 'PWM slider'; they are rate limits, so they apply to the SPEED slider.
IL and AL: the text says both 'have no effect if the VCF attack is at minimum', and describes AL as 'reducing fundamentals'; elsewhere AL is the envelope peak above the cutoffs.
SINE: described as 'generated by the VCF'; it comes from the VCO and bypasses the VCF.
Presets: '1152 presets' and '128 factory presets and 8 user banks', '1,024 editable', versus 'Editing ... BANKs 1 or 2' and backup files 'dd_bank_1.p and dd_bank_2.p' (older two-bank wording).
Bank select: CC 0 range 0-8 in the chart, but the text says '0 = User Bank 1, 1 = User Bank 2, 2 = Factory Bank'.
CC chart: CC 74 is listed as BRILLIANCE while global BRIL is CC 109 and HPF B is CC 73; RESH B is CC 119 out of sequence; square and saw switch order differs between layers (A 43/44, B 71/70).
Mod wheel destination DETUNE is given as CC 95, but the CC chart has DETUNE on CC 32 and nothing on CC 95.
Panel numbering restarts at 1 after control 45, while the text refers to 'switch 49' and 'slider 48'.
NUMBER OF VOICES 'does not affect MONOPHONIC or UNISON, as they are limited to 1 voice', while the UNISON text says it uses up to NUMBER OF VOICES voices.
Power: DC input listed as 12 V / 2 A; the supplied adapter is 12 V 2.5 A.
Between sources: preset count is 384 (3 banks) in 2020 launch reports, 256 on Thomann's page and 1152 in this manual; later firmware added banks.
Between sources: SOS (MK1) gives coarse tuning +6/-7 semitones; this manual says about +/-5.
Between sources: SOS calls the filter contour IL-AL-A-D-R with zero sustain and says the manual's ADR/ADSR labels are wrong; the MK2 manual still calls it ADR.
Between sources: Bonedo describes portamento as a slider only; the manual and panel show a P/G switch plus slider. Whether the switch has a centre off position is still unconfirmed.
Between sources: Bank 2 holds 'recreations of the original 14 CS-80 presets'; the CS-80 manual lists 11 presets per channel (21-22 names).

modelling_gaps.detail: Layer I/II reuse the CS-80 'ch1'/'ch2' ids and the shared controls keep their CS-80 ids so the files can be diffed. Labels follow the Deckard's Dream panel.
No keyboard, ribbon, ring modulator, tremolo/chorus, preset tone selector, memory panels, foot controller or external input. The MIDI input replaces the keyboard as 'kbd'.
Low and high halves act on a curve around MIDDLE OCTAVE across TRACKING WIDTH; modelled as one connection with the curve described in notes.
The per-patch wheel destination is modelled with switched connections for LFO depth, brilliance and PWM speed; the remaining destinations act on parameters directly.
The manual gives 50 mm depth; recorded as stated though it looks small for a unit with eight voice cards.
